turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess... I'm here because I just don't care about anything anymore. Like, anything at all. It's hard to even explain how empty it feels, but... well, I used to do so much, you know? I had these art classes that I was taking, and I'd get all my supplies out and actually feel something when I worked on a piece, but now the canvases are just sitting in the corner gathering dust and I can't even bring myself to look at them. 

And it's not just the art. I used to go to these board-game nights with people, like, we had this whole regular group, and we'd laugh and play for hours, but now the thought of going and sitting around a table and pretending to care about the rules or who is winning just feels... completely pointless. I don't even reply to their messages anymore. I used to love hiking, too, just getting out on the trails and being out in nature, but my boots haven't moved from the closet in I don't know how long. I was even supposed to get back to playing on my old recreational soccer team, and they kept asking if I was coming back for the season, but I just have absolutely zero interest. None. I don't care about the team, I don't care about the games. 

So instead, I just sit in my room. Day in and day out, I just sit there on my bed or in my chair. It’s like I’m just sitting there in the quiet while my whole life, everything that used to make me who I am, is just completely slipping away, and I don't even have it in me to care enough to try and stop it.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly states they 'don't care about anything anymore' and describes a complete loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities like art, board games, hiking, and soccer.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt this way before in your life, or is this the first time you've experienced these feelings?
turns.patient_response:
I mean... I don't think I've ever felt quite this bad before. Not like this. It's just... it's been going on for so long now. I remember exactly when it started, too, because it was right after the divorce. That was... gosh, it's been about 1 year and 11 months now. Almost two whole years of just... nothing. 

When he first left, I thought, okay, it's normal to be sad, right? You're supposed to grieve the end of a marriage. You cry, you eat ice cream, you watch sad movies, whatever people do. But then... it just never stopped. It didn't get better. The crying stopped, mostly, but it wasn't because I felt better, it was just because I ran out of whatever it is inside you that makes tears. And then it just turned into this... this heavy, gray nothingness. 

I kept thinking, "Next month will be better. I'll get back to the art next month. I'll call the board game group next month." But next month would come, and I'd still just be sitting on the edge of my bed staring at the wall. For an hour, sometimes two hours, just staring at the texture of the paint on the wall. And the seasons changed outside my window—I remember watching the leaves turn brown and fall off the tree across the street, and then the snow came, and then the leaves grew back, and I was still just sitting there. It's been almost two years of that. Twenty-three months of just watching the world happen outside my window while I slowly disappear inside this room. I just... I never thought it would last this long. I didn't know a person could feel this empty for 1 year and 11 months and still be breathing, you know?

turns.doctor_question: Beyond this feeling of emptiness and loss of interest, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep during these past two years?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um... yeah. I mean, my appetite is just... it's completely gone. Like, I don't even think about food anymore. I'll wake up, and I won't eat breakfast, and then lunchtime comes and goes, and I don't even notice. Sometimes the sun starts going down, and I realize I haven't had a single thing to eat all day, but even then, I just can't bring myself to care. 

When I do try to eat—because sometimes my mom will come over and she'll make me a sandwich or something and just sit there watching me until I take a bite—it's awful. It literally tastes like cardboard. There's no flavor, no joy in it. I used to love cooking, you know? I had all these spices and I'd try new recipes, but now... I might as well be chewing on paper. It's just a chore. A physical chore to swallow. 

And because of that, my clothes... they just don't fit anymore. I put on my favorite pair of jeans the other day—the ones I used to wear all the time, they used to fit perfectly, maybe even a little snug after the holidays—and they were just hanging off me. They were so loose they were sliding right down my hips. I actually had to take a hair tie and knot the waistband just so I could walk from my bedroom to the kitchen without them falling off. It's like I'm shrinking. My body is just... disappearing, just like everything else. I don't even know how much weight I've lost because I don't have a scale, but I can feel it in my bones. When I sit in my chair, my bones ache against the wood because there's just no padding left, you know? And I know I should probably try to eat something, maybe drink one of those protein shakes people talk about, but the thought of it just makes me feel exhausted. Everything is just so exhausting.

turns.doctor_question: During these long periods where you sit staring at the wall for hours, have you ever felt like you were losing touch with reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that weren't there, or perhaps feeling like your mind was completely blank and unable to process any thoughts at all?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um... yeah. I mean, it's not just my mind going blank, though that does happen sometimes where it's just like TV static in my head. But... there's something else. It's actually really hard to talk about because I know how it sounds, and I've been trying to just ignore it, but I can't. 

When I'm sitting there, staring at the wall... I hear this voice. It's a woman's voice, and it always comes from the exact same spot—the back right corner of my bedroom, near where the closet door is. The first time it happened, I actually got up and checked the closet because I thought maybe someone had broken into the house and was hiding in there, or maybe it was the neighbors outside and the sound was just carrying weirdly through the vents. But there was no one there. And the window was shut tight. 

But I still hear her. And she's not just mumbling or whispering where I can't make out the words. It's so clear. It sounds exactly as clear and as loud as if you were standing right next to my bed right now talking to me. She just keeps saying... she tells me that I ruined everything. Over and over. "You ruined everything. You ruined your life. You ruined your marriage." And then she tells me that I should just stay inside. That I shouldn't go out, I shouldn't let anyone see me, because I'm just a failure and I ruin things. 

And it's terrifying, honestly, because I know she's not physically there in the room, but my ears hear her. My brain hears her. I'll cover my ears with a pillow, or I'll pull the blanket all the way up over my head and try to hum to drown it out, but it doesn't matter because she's still just standing in that corner, telling me I should never leave this room again. And it makes it so much harder to even think about getting up or trying to eat or do anything, because she's right, you know? I did ruin everything. But hearing someone else say it, out loud, right in my own bedroom... it's just so loud, Doctor. It's so loud and I can't make her stop.

symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient expresses intense guilt and worthlessness, stating she is a failure and believes she 'ruined everything.'
symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient confirms experiencing her mind going blank, describing the sensation as being like 'TV static' in her head.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced these auditory hallucinations or similar feelings of losing touch with reality during any other periods of depression in your past, or is this the first time this has ever happened?
turns.patient_response:
I mean... it's actually kind of strange, because... well, she didn't just show up when I got this sad. It wasn't like the emptiness came and then the voice followed right after. There was actually this whole stretch of time, for weeks, right before the absolute worst of the depression really set in... where I was still doing okay, relatively speaking. Like, I could still cook sometimes. I remember making this big batch of spaghetti sauce, chopping all the garlic and onions and everything, and I was still answering texts from my friends, trying to keep up appearances and pretend things were normal. I wasn't just sitting on the edge of the bed staring at the wall yet. 

But she was already there. I was already hearing the voice from the corner of the room, even when I was just trying to stir a pot on the stove. And... and it wasn't just the voice, either. There was this whole thing with the hallway lights outside my door. I started noticing them flickering, and I completely believed—I mean, I was absolutely certain in my bones—that they were flashing specific signals about me. Like they were broadcasting to everyone in the building that I was a failure, or warning people about what I'd done. I would just stand there at my front door, looking through the little peephole for I don't even know how long, my eye just pressed right up against the glass, watching those fluorescent lights buzz and blink, trying to read the signals they were sending about me. 

And that went on for weeks. For weeks I was still functioning, still making food, still replying to people when they asked how I was doing, but my mind was already trapped with that voice and those lights. So it wasn't just when I was too depressed to move. It started before all that heavy, gray nothingness took over completely. I was already losing my grip while I was still trying to live a normal life.
